title: Redesign empty cart for fashion shoppers
persona: Rohan, product designer on Myntra checkout
scenario: Empty cart on Myntra is a dead screen, just an icon and a ‘shop now’ CTA. Behavioural data says 38% of returning users land on the cart even when they haven't added anything, scanning for wishlist items they half-remember. Your design lead wants 3 redesign concepts with a clear opinion on which one to ship, and one that you'd reject and why.
badPrompt: redesign the empty cart screen for myntra
badOutput:
Empty Cart Redesign

1. Add product recommendations.
2. Show wishlist items.
3. Show recently viewed products.

These will help users find products and increase engagement.

hints.title: Anchor the user behaviour
hints.body: Tell Claude the 38% behaviour: returning users use the cart as a wishlist re-entry point. Without this, Claude defaults to generic empty-state patterns.

hints.title: Force a rejected concept
hints.body: Demand one rejected concept WITH the reason. ‘Argue against one of your own ideas.’ This surfaces tradeoffs that a flat list of three hides.

checks.tip: Frame the artifact, redesign concepts, not specs.
Name the surface, empty cart, not just ‘cart’.
Anchor the user behaviour, 38% of returning users use cart as wishlist re-entry.
Specify the category, fashion, it changes empty-state norms.
Lock the count, 3 concepts. Otherwise Claude offers 7.
Demand a rejected concept with the reason. Adversarial framing surfaces tradeoffs.
Reference the design lead audience and the ‘pick one to ship’ ask.
Ask for the tradeoff reasoning, not just the recommendation.
Specify the structure, concept name + behaviour change + tradeoff.
Ask for low-fi descriptions, not just labels. Components, hierarchy, motion.

tipIfLow: Empty-state redesigns from AI default to generic patterns. The unlock is anchoring the specific user behaviour AND forcing a rejected concept. Adversarial framing, ‘argue against one of your own ideas’, surfaces tradeoffs a flat list hides.
goldPrompt: Act as a senior product designer at Myntra. I'm Rohan, designer on checkout. Empty cart is currently a dead screen (icon + 'shop now'). Behavioural data: 38% of returning users land on the cart with nothing added — they're scanning for half-remembered wishlist items. Output: 3 redesign concepts. For each: user-behaviour anchor, hero element, key interaction, expected impact metric. Then add ONE rejected concept WITH the reason it loses (e.g., adds friction, breaks browse flow). Format as a table. Lead must be able to ship one of these by next sprint.
